author: Ambiguous
resume_author: Funny thing about shit -- good things tend to grow out of it
text_post: My view is that the majority of people whether they're in a committed monogamous relationship or not still feel attraction or connection to people outside of that relationship. We are however trained to see commitment as one person and it's a romantic display of our love to that person to not sleep with (or otherwise invest deep feelings) towards anyone but them. Which, to me, is all backwards, we should never be repressing natural feelings towards anyone that isn't our partner and we shouldn't ask our partners to. What we should do is go about it the right ways, communicate, be honest make sure you and your current partner are on the same page and always respect each other, not just grab hold and say "mine!". For some that means monogamy and they're happy with it, but for those who are seeing other people and feeling an attraction and telling themselves "no I'm taken", seems to me it'd lead to some amount of resentment or possibly full out cheating if they're constantly trying to bury that part of themselves in order to prove their love.  The only commitment you need, in my opinion, is that when the shit hits the fan that person is there for you, and that they still put the same efforts into your relationship as when you started even if they have someone on the side. Either way I'd be setting out the exact parameters and always reassessing. I can't say I really agree with this for married people though, seems to defeat the purpose of your marriage, or the symbol that marriage is to most? That and it's risky to do after marriage if it doesn't work out. If someone is going to pursue an open relationship I think it should be from the start then if someone finds they can't handle it and want to back out they can do so before too much is invested. Everyone should know what they want and what they're getting into right off, which is hard with liars but if you end up seeing a few people on the side and your partner freaks after saying they were cool it's a pretty good indicator. It also helps weed out those who just see an open relationship as a way out of their suddenly boring one without actually leaving it.

text_post: I agree with the video mostly, particularly the part about trying to be everything for your partner or expecting them to be (lover, friend, support etc). I've actually brought up much the same thing in my own discussions on it. It is first off unreasonable to think that we can be everything for someone because we really can't, especially in a purely physical sense, but even in a emotional sense. There are things about my partner I will never even remotely grasp or understand and therefore can never play a role in, someone else probably can and does and in typical monogamous relationships this is just a friend or further and considered an infidelity. We always want to stop at the platonic stage and say it's not ok to fill any desire that crosses the platonic stage even if our partner can't realistically fill that desire. Stopping it does not REMOVE it though.  It always makes me think to the way we see friendships, we can have multiple friends and no one is getting hurt over you spending time with a different friend because obviously you have different interest and one friends might fill that while another doesn't....so why do we not see our personal relationships this way? It kind of stands to just drive us mad because we are trying to be everything for our partner in this fear that they will leave if we're not enough but at the same time realizing in ourselves that we maybe aren't getting everything we're looking for from them.  Also have to agree with the point about doing the forbidden, naturally a lot of people want to do what they're told not to do, so seems to me that you just don't dictate your partner like an object and they won't feel even more persuaded to do it. Whatever their choices they will not be TRYING to hurt you...unless they are just a terrible person then you figure that out and leave fast as you can....but overall if you hold mutual respect for each other that respect should, in my opinion, include them being free to make their own choices (or mistakes). You are of course still free to leave if you can't handle their actions but you are the one that has to be open about it, admit your insecurities, admit your hurt or distaste for something....it's your choice what action to take, it is NOT your choice to dictate the actions someone else takes.
